questions.problem:
Which of the matrices below does **not** have an inverse?

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 6 & 6\end{aligned}],\,F=[\begin{aligned}6 & 6 \\ 6 & 6\end{aligned}],\,G=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 \\ 4 & 4\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
- For the matrix $D$, we have

$$
det(D)=3\cdot 6-6\cdot 2=6.
$$

Because $det(D)\ne 0,$ we conclude that $D$ is invertible.

- For the matrix $F$, we have

$$
det(F)=6\cdot 6-6\cdot 6=0.
$$

Because $det(F)=0,$ we conclude that $F$ is not invertible.

- For the matrix $G$, we have

$$
det(G)=(-2)\cdot 4-4\cdot 2=-16.
$$

Because $det(G)\ne 0,$ we conclude that $G$ is invertible.

Therefore, only $F$ does not have an inverse.

questions.knowledge_point: Solving for a Variable in a Singular Matrix
questions.problem: If $P=[\begin{aligned}n & -8 \\ -2 & n\end{aligned}]$ is a singular matrix, calculate the value(s) of $n.$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix $P$ is singular if and only if $det(P)=0.$ Calculating the determinant, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(P) & =n\cdot n-(-2)\cdot (-8) \\  & ={n}^{2}-16.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the determinant equal to $0$ and solve for $n:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{n}^{2}-16 & =0 \\ {n}^{2} & =16 \\ n & =\pm 4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the values of $n$ are $n=\pm 4.$

questions.problem:
Which of the matrices below are singular?

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 6 \\ 1 & -3\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 7 & 5\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
- For the matrix $A$, we have

$$
det(A)=-2\cdot (-3)-1\cdot 6=0.
$$

Because $det(A)=0,$ we conclude that $A$ is not invertible. Since $A$ is a square matrix that is not invertible, we also say that $A$ is singular.

- The matrix $B$ is a $1\times 2$ matrix. So, it is not invertible. Since the matrix is not square, we can't say that it's singular.

- For the matrix $C$, we have

$$
det(C)=1\cdot 5-7\cdot 0=5.
$$

Because $det(C)\ne 0,$ we conclude that $C$ is invertible.

Therefore, only $A$ is singular.

questions.problem: If $A=[\begin{aligned}48 & a \\ a & 3\end{aligned}]$ is a singular matrix, calculate the value(s) of $a.$
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix $A$ is singular if and only if $det(A)=0.$ Calculating the determinant, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(A) & =48\cdot 3-a\cdot a \\  & =144-{a}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we set the determinant equal to $0$ and solve for $a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}144-{a}^{2} & =0 \\ {a}^{2} & =144 \\ a & =\pm 12\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the values of $a$ are $a=\pm 12.$

questions.problem:
If $B=[\begin{aligned}x-5 & x+3 \\ 2 & -3\end{aligned}]$
is a singular matrix, calculate the value of $x.$

$x=$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The matrix $B$ is singular if and only if $det(B)=0.$ Calculating the determinant, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =(x-5)\cdot (-3)-2\cdot (x+3) \\  & =-3x+15-2x-6 \\  & =-5x+9.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we set the determinant equal to $0$ and solve for $x:$

$$
\begin{aligned}-5x+9 & =0 \\ -5x & =-9 \\ x & =\frac{9}{5}\end{aligned}
$$
